### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **56** of **208** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **32** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4265176cf34d47055346443f483ba826bd117161` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6d09a2eae24df8ecacd0e684b4552f0ca27d66e9` — the merge of head `8149b3d240e97680ab25dc5da74241c05816d87b` into base `4265176cf34d47055346443f483ba826bd117161`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6d09a2eae24df8ecacd0e684b4552f0ca27d66e9 && git checkout 6d09a2eae24df8ecacd0e684b4552f0ca27d66e9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4265176cf34d47055346443f483ba826bd117161 8149b3d240e97680ab25dc5da74241c05816d87b && git checkout -B drift-repro 4265176cf34d47055346443f483ba826bd117161 && git merge --no-ff 8149b3d240e97680ab25dc5da74241c05816d87b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4265176cf34d47055346443f483ba826bd117161
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8149b3d240e97680ab25dc5da74241c05816d87b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cli/src/utils/collect-docs.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/collect-docs.package-docs.test.ts, packages/cli/test/normalized-call-sites.test.ts + packages/cli/src/utils/artifact-packages.ts (`artifactPackages`: the `bodies[index]` position IS the `packages[i]` position, 1:1 map), packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts (`declaredDependencyIds`, `resolveArtifactPackageEntries`), packages/core/src/stack-collections.ts (`declaredPackageEntries`), packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts (the residual top-level rule the owner arm rests on), packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts (`manifest: 'preserve'` copy-removal and its three conditions), docs/adr/0051-inline-metadata-views-in-docs.md §3.3 and §3.5 step 3, docs/adr/0046-package-docs-as-metadata.md §3.3, skills/objectstack-ui/rules/pages.md (the follow-up owed), .changeset/27090-embed-ref-package-scope.md

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset, identical). Inputs: card #27090 body and all three comments (triage `6461907878`, claim `6465113081`, os-dev-report `6466645930`), PR #27204 body, file list and `git diff origin/main...pr27204` (merge base `6866e2e7`, 4 files, +259/-38), and the check-runs on this head. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Yardstick: triage `6461907878` — the embed is judged against the package that ships the doc, plus what that package declares it depends on; not "anything in the artifact".

1. **`lintMetadataEmbeds(docs, own, dependencies = [])` — one map builder over `[...dependency bodies, ...own]`.** Right. One builder, no second map, no new manifest key (the claim's two ⛔s hold). Dependencies first and owner last is the correct `Map` precedence (owner wins a shared name). Every pre-existing one-stack caller (`collect-docs.test.ts` ×2) is unchanged in signature and scope.
2. **Dependency edge = `declaredDependencyIds(body)` over the artifact's own bodies, direct only, one-way, self excluded, an id the artifact does not carry dropped.** Right. `declaredDependencyIds` reads `manifest.dependencies` (`packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts:196`), the same field `resolveArtifactPackageEntries` orders the load by (ADR-0130 D5), and `preserve` writes the assembled body as manifest fields + collections, so `body.dependencies` and `body.objects` are on one record. Direct-only matches ADR-0051 §3.3 ("own package, then its dependencies") and ADR-0046 §3.3 ("the package's docs plus its dependencies' docs"). Read and confirmed in the diff's `embedScope`: `dep.index !== index`, `bodyById.get(id)` only.
3. **Widening arm — a package's directory docs and inline body docs (`entry.all`) judged against its body + declared deps.** Right, and it is the card's acceptance 1 and 2 (pinned: own object builds; undeclared sibling refused; declared sibling builds; one-way). The measured premise is pinned too (`artifact.objects` undefined under `preserve`), so the test cannot pass vacuously against a flattened copy.
4. **Narrowing arm (a) — inline body docs with a dead embed now refuse.** Right and real: on `main` the package pass judged `entry.fromDisk` only, and the stack pass judged the top-level `docs`, which a two-package `preserve` artifact does not carry (stack.zod.ts copy-removal, conditions 1–3). A dead body-doc embed was therefore unjudged. Correctly declared as BREAKING.
5. **Narrowing arm (b) — in an artifact that keeps a flattened top level (a reconciled composition, condition 3 failing), a non-owner package doc embedding an undeclared sibling's item now refuses.** Right: that is the ruling's own sentence. Correctly declared.
6. **Stack-level docs (`stackScoped`) judged against `[stack, ownerBody]` + the owner's deps when `flatDocsOwner` resolves; `[stack]` alone otherwise.** Right. The card's Target says stack-level docs are judged against the stack's own definitions; adding the owner body is the #22190 consequence (those docs ship on that body). A single-package stack: `flatDocsOwner` is `undefined`, scope `[stack]`, issue list unmoved — acceptance 3, pinned.
7. **The owner package's own docs reach the top level too (`own = [stack, body]` when `index === flatOwner.index`).** Right for what the top level actually carries in an ADR-0130 artifact: residual items no body claims, which `MetadataPlugin.registerUnclaimedTopLevel` registers under the artifact's `manifest.id`, i.e. under this very package (app-plugin.ts docblock, read). The restated link/embed test pins exactly that shape (a top-level flow owned by nobody, `core` = `manifest.id`). **One corner is wider than the ruling's sentence** and the PR names it in its acceptance notes: in a *reconciled* composition the top level also holds the flattened copies of sibling items the bodies claim, so the owner's docs can still embed an undeclared sibling's item through that copy while a non-owner's cannot. That copy is registered under the sibling, not the owner, so render would resolve it only through a declared edge. Bounded (owner package only, `objectConflict: 'merge'`/`'override'` compositions only), strictly narrower than `main` (which admitted it for every package), and no fixture in this repo or HotCRM carries it. Not a FAIL; escalated in ③ with the sharper rule named.
8. **Refusal text names the judged scope** ("this package" / "this package or its declared dependencies (IDS)"). Right; IDS lists carried deps only, which is the set judged. The did-you-mean suffix stays.
9. **Docblocks of `collectDocsFromSrc`, `lintMetadataEmbeds`, `collectAndLintDocs` rewritten to say links resolve artifact-wide and embeds do not.** Right; the previous text ("the same scope `lintMetadataEmbeds` already uses") would have been false after this diff.
10. **Census row `utils/collect-docs.ts :: stack.books` → `top-level`.** Right as a classification: `lintDocNavTargets` does `addBooks(stack.books)` AND `addBooks(body.books)` over `artifactPackages(stack)` (collect-docs.ts head :1134–1138), so the top-level read is one half of a union by design. The read is pre-existing on `main`; the row is needed at this head because the diff removed the `stack.objects/flows/permissions` reads (now `source[key]` over a non-stack receiver) and shifted `codeOnly`'s quote parity. I read `codeOnly` (census.head.ts :156–187): it scans a backtick literal to the next unescaped backtick, so a template literal nested inside another's `${}` does throw it out of phase — the dev's reading of the masker defect is credible and the gate was indeed false-green on `main` for this file. The masker is not fixed here (out of the claim's file surface, class a finding) — see ③.
11. **Public surface.** `@objectstack/cli`: `lintMetadataEmbeds` is an `export` of an internal util, not a package entry; its second parameter widened to a union and a third optional parameter added — source-compatible for every existing caller. New exported `interface EmbedDependency`. Nothing in `packages/spec`; `check:api-surface` is not implicated. `@objectstack/core` is already a dependency of cli (`workspace:*`), and `declaredDependencyIds` is exported via `export * from './artifact-packages.js'`.

Nothing in the diff lands outside the three hits plus the changeset; no governed path (Queue Guard green).

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/27090-embed-ref-package-scope.md`: `'@objectstack/cli': patch`, BREAKING banner, both declaration lines, one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with a reason. Right: a non-protocol accept-set change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` with its banner and disposition (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3). `cli` is the only package the diff moves (`core` is read, not changed). `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset — identical, and the narrowing is real (①4, ①5). `yes (widening)` would have been false.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` — accepted. No Zod key, accepted value or metadata type moves; the `docs` item's content schema is unchanged; what moves is the build-time liveness check's resolution scope, which ADR-0051 §3.5 step 3 already specified as "the package and its dependencies". The narrowing is carried, correctly, by the Clause-② arm.
- ADR-0087 `no-migration-prescription`: the body carries a remedy (declare the dependency / move the doc / fix the name), which is a doc-authoring fix, not a consumer-code rewrite; consistent with the marker's own rule (statement-against-statement).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`Skills-docs: follow-up owed`** — `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/pages.md` :396–398 says the referenced item "must exist in this package — a dead same-package reference fails the build". After this PR that sentence is incomplete (declared dependencies now resolve). `skills/**` is Tier H, outside this claim: **escalated to the seat — a docs card on `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/pages.md` is owed; no other prose surface states the old rule** (grep of `content/docs`, `skills`, `apps/docs` for "exist in this package" / "metadata-embed-ref": only this page).
- **os-dev-report `out_of_scope_findings` [0], class a — the census masker.** `codeOnly` in `packages/cli/test/normalized-call-sites.test.ts` loses its place on a nested template literal, so `every top-level read of a package-owned key in src is classified` was green on `main` while blanking four reads in collect-docs.ts. Pre-existing, not introduced here; the PR's new row is correct at this head but the gate's coverage of OTHER files is equally parity-dependent. **Escalated to the seat — a card for the masker (fix `codeOnly` to track `${…}` nesting, with a `--self-test`/fixture case).** Not a FAIL: the gate is a test, not a required-check rename, and the defect is reachable from `main`.
- **①7 corner (owner package + reconciled composition).** The sharper rule is "the top level's *unclaimed* items" — the exact set `registerUnclaimedTopLevel` registers under `manifest.id` — rather than the whole top level. **Escalated to the seat as a follow-up question, not a defect of this PR:** it is the card's own "stack-level docs against the stack's own definitions" applied to the body those docs ship on, it is narrower than `main`, and the PR declares it in writing.
- `open_questions`: `[]` on the report. Nothing further to answer.
- Draft state: the PR is a draft, owned by the seat; nothing here arms it.

Check-runs on `8149b3d2…` (read after every run concluded; 52 runs, 0 pending, 0 failed): `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (8/8 shards), `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `PR-body guards` all `success`; `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI` `skipped` (no `ui/` path in the diff); the opt-in and scheduled runs `skipped`. The gate verdicts are green.
